p.i: Dispulit omnipotens, sedesque excussit ad imas Multa reluctantes, belloque resistere adortos. Conueniunt, illis longaeua in secula poenis Excercere animas hominum data cura nocentes; Quos vbi confertos simul, atque in iussa paratos Vidit ab accenso Dux talia pectore rumpit.

Nunc validis nitendum animis, nunc robore firmo O socij, ne noster honos, & gloria cedat, Aequalesque Deo vinci patiamur inertes, Cernitis, vt pelagi tot vasta per aequora vectus Quiqueiae[?] Ligur extremas penetrauit ad oras? Iam ritus dabit ille nouos, antiquaque sacra Destruet, aequatisque solo nos trudet ab aris, Nostra etiam celebri victor captiua triumpho Credo equidem simulacra vehet, vinctisque catenis Ante rotas Erebi densa ibimus agmine Reges Terrarum domini, & coeli stellantis alumni. Nos qui bella Deum, socialiaque agmina contra, Contulimus, paribusque vltro certauimus armis, Nos igitur? Nos mortali vincemur ab hoste? O, tantum prohibete nefas restinguite flammas Serpentes, lapsisque simul succurrite rebus, Tollite pacatas ventis pugnantibus vndas, Inque ipso gentem, & naues submergite portu, Compositam pacem, vanumque infringite foedus, Quod socios si bella inter, Liguremque seratis Maxima res effecta, timorque euanuit omnis,

page.notes: The verse is set in italic throughout. Paragraph division follows the single indent before "Nunc". Quiqueiae and the stanza openings are uncertain in places. The word "Nec" at the lower right is a catchword, and it is also listed above as a note line; only the catchword element should carry it.
